label: Sequencing reads
definition: Raw or processed reads produced by a high-throughput DNA or RNA sequencer, carrying per-base sequence and associated quality scores, distinct from classical Sanger sequence traces.

label: Short-read sequencing data
definition: High-throughput sequencing reads of typically 50-300 bp produced by short-read platforms such as Illumina, including raw base-called FASTQ files and paired-end read pairs from DNA-seq, RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and related assays.

label: Long-read sequencing data
definition: Sequencing reads of multi-kilobase to megabase length produced by single-molecule platforms such as Oxford Nanopore Technologies or PacBio HiFi, enabling direct phasing, full-length isoform reconstruction, and base-modification detection.

label: Cell barcode and UMI data
definition: Per-read oligonucleotide tags comprising a cell barcode that identifies the cell of origin and a unique molecular identifier (UMI) that marks the individual captured molecule, used in droplet-based single-cell and spatial sequencing workflows prior to demultiplexing and count-matrix generation.

label: Basecalled sequence data
definition: Nucleotide sequence reads produced by signal-level basecalling of raw electrical signal data from nanopore sequencers (Oxford Nanopore Technologies) or fluorescent intensity data from PacBio SMRT sequencers, including per-base quality scores, read lengths, and optionally modification probability arrays, as output by Dorado, Guppy, or CCS.

label: Single-cell omics data
definition: Molecular measurements made at the resolution of individual cells, encompassing single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin accessibility, surface proteomics, and multimodal omics data types.

label: Single-cell count matrix
definition: A sparse matrix of per-cell feature counts (genes, peaks, proteins, or other quantified molecules) from droplet-based or plate-based single-cell sequencing, organized as cells-by-features with associated barcode and feature metadata, as produced by tools such as Cell Ranger, STARsolo, Alevin-fry, or Kallisto bustools.

label: Cell barcode annotation
definition: A per-cell metadata table linking cell barcodes to assigned cluster identifiers, cell type labels, QC metrics (total counts, gene detection rate, mitochondrial fraction), batch or sample identifiers, and inferred doublet status from a single-cell omics experiment.

label: Cell embedding
definition: Low-dimensional coordinate representation of individual cells produced by dimensionality reduction methods (PCA, UMAP, t-SNE, diffusion maps, or scVI latent space) applied to single-cell omics data, used for visualization, trajectory inference, and cluster identification.

label: Cell trajectory
definition: An ordered arrangement of cells along a developmental or differentiation continuum, represented as pseudotime values, branching tree topology, or lineage graph derived from single-cell omics data using methods such as Monocle, RNA velocity, PAGA, or Palantir.

label: RNA velocity data
definition: Paired count matrices of spliced and unspliced (nascent) RNA transcripts derived from single-cell RNA-seq, together with estimated velocity vectors that predict the direction and rate of future gene expression changes within each cell, as computed by scVelo, velocyto, or UniTVelo.

label: Spatial transcriptomics data
definition: A gene expression count matrix paired with physical spatial coordinates for each measurement location (spot, bead, pixel, or segmented cell) within a tissue section, as produced by platforms such as 10x Visium, Slide-seq, MERFISH, seqFISH, or HDST, enabling linkage of molecular profiles to tissue histology.

label: Single-cell ATAC-seq data
definition: Per-cell chromatin accessibility fragment files and associated peak-by-cell count matrices from single-cell ATAC-seq experiments, used to profile open chromatin regions at single-cell resolution.

label: Mass cytometry data
definition: Per-cell mass-based measurements of 30-50 protein markers from CyTOF (cytometry by time-of-flight) experiments, providing high-dimensional single-cell protein abundance profiles without the spectral spillover limitations of conventional flow cytometry.

label: Multiplex tissue image
definition: Spatially resolved, highly multiplexed protein or RNA expression images of tissue sections acquired by CODEX, Imaging Mass Cytometry (IMC), MIBI-TOF, or cyclic immunofluorescence (CyCIF), providing simultaneous single-cell resolution visualization of 20-60 molecular markers.

label: Epigenomics data
definition: Genome-wide measurements of epigenetic marks or chromatin states, including protein-DNA binding, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and three-dimensional genome organization.

label: ChIP-seq data
definition: Sequencing reads from chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing experiments, used to map genome-wide protein-DNA binding sites, histone modification patterns, or transcription factor occupancy.

label: Chromatin accessibility profile
definition: Genome-wide measurement of open chromatin regions from ATAC-seq, FAIRE-seq, or DNase-seq, representing the set of accessible regulatory elements - including promoters, enhancers, and insulators - in a bulk cell population or individual cell.

label: ChIP-seq peak data
definition: Genomic intervals identified as significantly enriched for a chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) or CUT&RUN/CUT&TAG signal relative to a background or input control, annotated with peak coordinates, summit positions, fold enrichment, and statistical scores as produced by MACS2/3, SPP, or SEACR.

label: DNA methylation data
definition: Base-resolution or CpG-level cytosine methylation measurements recording methylation fraction and sequencing coverage at each genomic position, derived from whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), enzymatic methyl-seq (EM-seq), reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS), or nanopore direct sequencing with modification calling.

label: Chromatin contact matrix
definition: Pairwise genome-wide interaction frequency data between genomic loci derived from chromosome conformation capture experiments (Hi-C, Micro-C, in situ Hi-C, or Dip-C), stored as a symmetric matrix binned at a defined resolution (typically 1 kb to 1 Mb) and used to detect TADs, loops, and compartments.

label: Chromatin domain data
definition: Genomic coordinates of topologically associating domains (TADs), sub-TAD loop anchors, compartment boundaries, or insulator elements inferred from chromatin contact matrices, representing the hierarchical three-dimensional organization of the genome as detected by tools such as HiCExplorer, TADbit, or Juicer.

label: Base modification data
definition: Per-site probability scores or binary calls for DNA or RNA base modifications - including 5-methylcytosine (5mC), 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), N6-methyladenine (m6A), and pseudouridine - derived from direct nanopore sequencing basecalling with modification models or from chemical conversion sequencing methods.

label: Variant call data
definition: Structured records of genetic variants (SNVs, indels, MNVs) at specific genomic positions, including reference and alternate allele sequences, per-sample genotype calls, allele depths, and variant quality metrics, typically stored in Variant Call Format (VCF) or BCF as produced by GATK HaplotypeCaller, DeepVariant, FreeBayes, or Clair3.

label: Structural variant data
definition: Genomic rearrangements larger than approximately 50 bp - including deletions, duplications, inversions, translocations, mobile element insertions, and copy number variants - detected by paired-end read-depth analysis, split-read alignment, or long-read sequencing using tools such as Manta, LUMPY, Sniffles, PBSV, or SVABA.

label: Copy number variation data
definition: A genome-segmented profile of DNA copy number states derived from read-depth normalization, allele-frequency analysis, or array comparative genomic hybridization, annotating genomic intervals with estimated integer or fractional copy number, log2 ratio, and associated confidence, as produced by CNVkit, GATK CNV, or PURPLE.

label: Phased genotype data
definition: Variant calls with haplotype-resolved allele assignments linking specific alleles to paternal or maternal chromosomal copies, produced by statistical phasing (SHAPEIT, BEAGLE), population-based phasing, trio-based phasing, or long-read sequencing approaches (WhatsHap, HapCUT2), enabling haplotype-aware downstream analyses.

label: Somatic variant data
definition: Tumor-specific (somatic) mutations - including single-nucleotide variants, small indels, structural rearrangements, and copy number alterations - identified by comparing tumor sequencing to a matched or unmatched normal sample using tools such as Mutect2, Strelka2, VarScan2, or DRAGEN somatic pipeline.

label: GWAS summary statistics
definition: Genome-wide association study results comprising per-variant effect size estimates, standard errors, p-values, allele frequencies, and sample sizes across millions of variants, used for polygenic score calculation, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization, and LD score regression.

label: Allele frequency spectrum
definition: The distribution of derived or minor allele frequencies across segregating sites in one or more population samples, serving as the primary summary statistic for demographic inference, neutrality tests, and population genetics simulation.

label: Linkage disequilibrium data
definition: Pairwise LD statistics (r², D') between genetic variants computed from population-scale genotype panels, used in GWAS fine-mapping, conditional analysis, LD pruning, imputation reference panel construction, and polygenic score development.

label: Population structure data
definition: Ancestry proportion coefficients, principal component projections, or admixture fractions inferred from genome-wide variant data, used to characterize genetic relationships among individuals and populations and to correct for stratification in association studies.

label: Deep mutational scanning data
definition: Fitness or functional scores for thousands of individual amino acid or nucleotide variants in a protein or regulatory element, derived from a pooled mutagenesis and selection experiment, used as ground truth for variant effect prediction benchmarks.

label: Taxonomic profile
definition: A quantitative table of microbial taxonomic abundances (OTU or ASV table, species or strain abundance profile) from 16S rRNA, ITS, or shotgun metagenomic sequencing, recording relative or absolute abundances across taxonomy ranks as produced by QIIME 2, DADA2, MetaPhlAn, Bracken, or Kraken2.

label: Metagenome-assembled genome
definition: A draft genome sequence reconstructed by binning contigs from a metagenomic assembly based on tetranucleotide frequency, read coverage, and taxonomic markers, representing a putative single organism from a complex microbial community, as produced by MetaBAT2, MaxBin2, CONCOCT, or DAS Tool.

label: Functional metagenomics profile
definition: An abundance table of functional gene categories (KEGG orthologs, COG/EGGNOG clusters, EC numbers, CAZy families, or antibiotic resistance genes) annotated from metagenomic reads or assembled genes, quantifying the metabolic and functional potential of a microbial community using tools such as HUMAnN, eggNOG-mapper, or Prokka.

label: Genome assembly graph
definition: A graph-based representation of a genome assembly encoding sequence overlaps, contig connectivity, and alternative assembly paths - including string graphs, de Bruijn graphs, and assembly graphs in GFA format - produced by assemblers such as Hifiasm, Flye, Verkko, or wtdbg2 from long-read or Hi-C data.

label: Genome variation graph
definition: A graph-based reference structure encoding population-level sequence variation - including SNVs, indels, and structural variants - as a directed or bidirected sequence graph (GFA or rGFA format), enabling haplotype-aware read alignment and variant genotyping using tools such as vg, Minigraph-Cactus, or PGGB.

label: Protein structure prediction
definition: Computationally predicted three-dimensional protein or protein complex coordinates accompanied by per-residue confidence scores (pLDDT) and predicted aligned error (PAE) matrices, as produced by AlphaFold2, ESMFold, RoseTTAFold, ColabFold, or AlphaFold-Multimer.

label: Proteomics quantification matrix
definition: A matrix of protein or peptide abundance values across samples derived from label-free quantification, TMT/iTRAQ isobaric labeling, SILAC, or data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry-based proteomics, as produced by MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, FragPipe, DIA-NN, or Spectronaut.

label: Post-translational modification data
definition: Site-level quantification of protein post-translational modifications (phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation, glycosylation) combining peptide identification with stoichiometric measurements from enriched LC-MS/MS experiments.

label: DIA-MS spectral library
definition: A reference library of fragment ion spectra, precursor masses, and isoelectric retention times used by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) tools such as Spectronaut, DIA-NN, or OpenSWATH to identify and quantify peptides in sample runs.

label: Multi-omics dataset
definition: Paired or jointly profiled measurements from two or more molecular assay types - such as transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, or genomics - on matched samples or individual cells, enabling cross-modal integration and holistic analysis of molecular phenotypes using frameworks such as MOFA+, Seurat WNN, or MultiVI.

label: Polygenic risk score
definition: A weighted linear sum of allelic dosages at genome-wide loci quantifying an individual's inherited genetic risk for a complex trait or disease, derived from genome-wide association study summary statistics and linkage disequilibrium reference panels using methods such as PRSice-2, LDpred2, PRS-CS, or lassosum.

label: Tumor mutational burden
definition: A quantitative measure of the total number of somatic mutations per megabase of interrogated genome or exome sequence in a tumor sample, calculated from targeted panel, whole-exome, or whole-genome sequencing and used as a biomarker for immunotherapy response.

label: Machine learning data
definition: Structured numerical data prepared as input to or produced as output from a machine learning model, encompassing embedding vectors, feature matrices, serialized model weights, and training labels.

label: Biological embedding
definition: A fixed-length dense vector representation of a biological sequence (DNA, RNA, or protein), structure, cell, or molecule learned by a neural language model or deep learning encoder (such as ESM-2, DNABERT, scGPT, or Enformer), capturing semantic relationships for downstream tasks such as function prediction, similarity search, or generative modeling.

label: Trained model
definition: Serialized parameters, weights, and architecture specification of a trained machine learning or deep learning model for biological data analysis - including classifiers, regressors, generative models, and foundation models - stored in formats such as HDF5, PyTorch .pt, TensorFlow SavedModel, or ONNX for inference or transfer learning.

label: Machine learning feature matrix
definition: A sample-by-feature numerical matrix prepared for supervised or unsupervised machine learning, where features may be heterogeneous (genomic, clinical, imaging-derived, or proteomic) and are distinct from a raw expression count matrix.

label: Training labels
definition: Class labels, continuous target values, or structured annotations paired with a feature matrix or biological sequence dataset, defining the learning objective for supervised machine learning model training.

label: Flow cytometry data
definition: Per-event fluorescence intensity measurements across multiple channels from flow cytometry or FACS experiments, stored as FCS files and used as input to gating, population identification, and dimensionality reduction workflows.

label: Fluorescence microscopy image
definition: Multichannel fluorescence images acquired by widefield, confocal, or super-resolution microscopy, storing spatial intensity distributions of fluorescently labeled biological structures across one or more spectral channels and one or more z-planes.

label: High-content screening data
definition: Plate-level fluorescence microscopy images from automated imaging systems in cell-based screening experiments, combined with well-level compound or perturbation metadata, used for morphological profiling and phenotypic drug discovery.

label: Imaging-derived phenotype
definition: Quantitative features extracted from medical images (MRI, CT, PET) by radiomics pipelines or deep learning models, used as phenotypic measurements in imaging-genetics studies and as biomarker inputs for clinical prediction models.

label: sgRNA library
definition: A designed set of guide RNA sequences with their intended genomic target coordinates and gene assignments, used as a reference to map reads from pooled CRISPR screens or as input to guide design and off-target scoring tools.

label: CRISPR screen read counts
definition: A guide-RNA-by-sample count matrix from a pooled CRISPR knockout, activation, or base-editing screen, in which each value represents the number of sequencing reads mapping to a given guide RNA in a given sample or time point.

label: Drug-target interaction data
definition: Quantitative binding affinity measurements (Kd, Ki, IC₅₀) between small-molecule compounds and molecular targets, used as training data for virtual screening models, drug-target interaction prediction, and structure-activity relationship analysis.

label: Drug sensitivity data
definition: Cell-line or patient-level dose-response curves and derived sensitivity metrics (AUC, IC₅₀, EC₅₀) from pharmacological perturbation experiments, used as input to pharmacogenomics modeling, combination synergy analysis, and drug repurposing workflows.

label: Structured phenotype data
definition: Machine-readable coded clinical observations, diagnoses, laboratory values, and procedures for cohort individuals, such as HPO-annotated phenotype profiles, OMOP CDM tables, or ICD-coded disease records, used as input to genotype-phenotype association studies.

label: Survival data
definition: Time-to-event data for a clinical cohort including an event indicator (observed or censored) and elapsed time, used as input to Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression, and competing risks models.
